title: Enhanced Diffusion through Multivalency
authors: Bartoš L; Lund M; Vácha R
one_liner_zh: 该文通过计算机模拟研究多价颗粒在表面/纤维上的1D/2D扩散加速现象，虽涉及多价结合与受体互作，但对象为颗粒-表面体系而非蛋白质-DNA或TF-DNA，方法为通用模拟，对TF-DNA动态结合机理建模有间接启发。
abstract:
In multivalent systems, multiple ligands from one entity simultaneously bind to multiple receptors on another entity. These interactions are of crucial significance in a wide range of biological and technological mechanisms, encompassing selectivity, host recognition, viral penetration, therapeutic delivery, as well as the adhesion phenomena found in cells, polymers, and nanoparticles. In this study, we used computer simulations to investigate 1D and 2D diffusion of adsorbed particles with varying valency but with the same overall affinity to the host. We demonstrate a remarkable diffusion acceleration for particles with increasing valency. Non-diffusing monovalent particle can attain almost unrestricted diffusion when becoming multivalent while retaining its affinity for the host tether or surface. Moreover, diffusion of multivalent particles with rigid ligand distribution can be controlled by patterned host receptors. Our results have practical implications for the design of fast-diffusing particles that maintain a strong affinity for target surfaces or molecules.

TOC Graphic

Significance

We investigated how the number of binding sites (referred to as valency) on particles or entities impacts their movement when attached to surfaces or filaments. Valency can be understood as how many “hands” a particle has to grip the surface. Surprisingly, particles with more “hands” move faster if they hold onto the surface with the same strength. Furthermore, the motion of these particles can be controlled by designing surfaces with specific patterns that the “hands” can grasp. This means that we can design particles that move rapidly while remaining attached to the desired locations. These findings hold promise for applications like drug delivery and materials technology, and for understanding biological processes.
abstract_zh:
在多价系统中，一个实体上的多个配体同时与另一个实体上的多个受体结合。这些相互作用在广泛的生物和技术机制中具有至关重要的意义，包括选择性、宿主识别、病毒侵入、治疗递送，以及细胞、聚合物和纳米颗粒中的粘附现象。在本研究中，我们使用计算机模拟来研究具有不同价数但总体对宿主亲和力相同的吸附颗粒的一维和二维扩散。我们展示了随着价数增加，颗粒扩散显著加速的现象。非扩散的单价颗粒在变为多价并保持其对宿主系链或表面的亲和力时，几乎可以实现无限制的扩散。此外，具有刚性配体分布的多价颗粒的扩散可以通过图案化的宿主受体来控制。我们的研究结果对于设计既能快速扩散又能对目标表面或分子保持强亲和力的颗粒具有实际意义。

目录图

意义

我们研究了颗粒或实体上结合位点数量（称为价数）如何影响其附着在表面或细丝上的运动。价数可以理解为颗粒有多少只“手”来抓住表面。令人惊讶的是，如果颗粒以相同的强度抓住表面，拥有更多“手”的颗粒移动得更快。此外，这些颗粒的运动可以通过设计具有特定图案的表面来控制，这些图案可供“手”抓握。这意味着我们可以设计出既能快速移动又能保持在目标位置的颗粒。这些发现为药物递送和材料技术等应用以及理解生物过程带来了希望。
